blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-08-11 at Ethereum block 25730449. Ethereum frxUSD proxy 0xcacd6fd266af91b8aed52accc382b4e165586e29 resolves as Frax USD / frxUSD and delegates to verified FrxUSD implementation 0x0000000048d2c8baf31742f6765383278bada4d5. The implementation ABI exposes freeze, freezeMany, thaw, thawMany, pause/unpause, isFrozen, and freezer-role administration. Current reads returned isPaused() = false and isFrozen(0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001) = false, while Blockscout log queries from start block 21543360 through 25730449 returned no AccountFrozen or AccountThawed events. The direct freeze capability is present even though no freeze/thaw event has been observed yet.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: frxUSD has native issuance on Ethereum and Fraxtal, Fraxtal canonical-side lockbox and L2 bridge machinery, and established LayerZero/FraxZero OFT representations on other chains. The reviewed cross-chain routes depend on external messaging, endpoint configuration, peer/DVN/rate-limit settings, and lock/mint or burn/mint contracts outside issuer-native redemption, so Pharos scores the overall route as external lock/mint. The Tempo deployment is retained but fail-closed as unresolved because its native-versus-bridge architecture and production status are not reconciled by the reviewed primary sources.

routes.reviewNote: Tempo frxUSD is live at the observed TIP-20 address and exposes Frax USD metadata, but its classification is fail-closed. Frax's current Tempo architecture documents FraxOFTMintableAdapterTIP20, FraxOFTUpgradeableTempo, LayerZero, supply-tracking, and a Mainnet (Presto) status of Coming Soon, while a separate Frax project update reports a Tempo mainnet launch. The reviewed evidence therefore does not establish whether this address is a canonical native issuance route, a bridge representation, or a staged deployment; no native mint authority or bridge controller is inferred.
